original_text: Organs of Flowering Plants We will be using the flowering plant as our model for understanding plant structure and organization. Most flowering plants have a root system (made of the roots) and a shoot system (made of stem and leaves) Most typical plants feature 3 vegetative organs, concerned with growth and nutrition Roots, stems, leaves Flowers, seeds and fruits are involved with reproduction, not growth and nutrition.
explanation: Flowering plants serve as the standard model for studying plant structure and organization. The body of a flowering plant is divided into two primary systems: the root system (comprising the roots) and the shoot system (comprising the stem and leaves). The plant possesses three vegetative organs that are responsible for growth and nutrition: the roots, stems, and leaves. Other plant organs, specifically flowers, seeds, and fruits, are specialized structures involved in reproduction rather than vegetative growth or nutrition.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a vegetative organ of a plant concerned with growth and nutrition?
questions.exp: The three vegetative organs concerned with plant growth and nutrition are the roots, stems, and leaves. Flowers, fruits, and seeds are involved in reproduction.

questions.q: What are the two primary systems that make up the structure of a flowering plant?
opts: The primary system and the secondary system
The vascular system and the ground system
The root system and the shoot system
The vegetative system and the reproductive system
questions.exp: Most flowering plants are structurally organized into a root system (roots) and a shoot system (stems and leaves).
